text: Silicon has a Kerr index n₂ roughly 230× larger than silica, yet Si₃N₄ is often preferred for Kerr-effect photonic processing at 1550 nm. Why?
choices: Silicon suffers strong two-photon absorption (nonlinear figure of merit ≈ 0.4 < 1), while Si₃N₄ has essentially no TPA at 1550 nm
Si₃N₄ has a much larger n₂ than silicon
Si₃N₄ has a much larger χ⁽²⁾ than silicon
explanation: Silicon's large χ⁽³⁾ is accompanied by two-photon absorption at 1550 nm, giving a figure of merit n₂/(λβ_TPA) ≈ 0.4 < 1 that limits nonlinear processing; Si₃N₄ has negligible TPA (FOM ≫ 1). Silicon is actually transparent at 1550 nm, Si₃N₄'s n₂ is smaller (not larger), and χ⁽²⁾ is irrelevant to the Kerr (χ⁽³⁾) effect.
